title: "Getting help"
description: "Who to ask, and where the communities are."

## Who to ask

| If you need | Ask |
|---|---|
| Advice on your assurance level, or a level dispute resolved | The Analytical Quality and Assurance Lead |
| A critical friend for your analysis | Your team lead in the first instance |
| Advice on official statistics | The Head of Profession for Statistics |
| Business Critical registration | The Data Science, Advanced Analytics and Statistics team |
| Information governance advice, or help with personal data | The information governance function. Ask before the work starts, not at sign-off |
| Help with analytical code, testing or reproducibility | The owners of the [Analytical Code Assurance Playbook](https://nhsbsa-data-analytics.github.io/nhsbsa-analytical-code-assurance-playbook) |

Each row names a role or a team rather than a person, so that a change of post holder is not a
change to this playbook. Who currently holds each one is in the governance and management framework.
If you cannot work out who to approach, start with your team lead. If that does not settle it,
write to [analyticalassurance@nhsbsa.nhs.uk](mailto:analyticalassurance@nhsbsa.nhs.uk). That
mailbox covers this playbook, the assurance level decision sheet and the Business Critical
templates, and will point you at the right person for anything else.

## Communities of practice

### Coffee and Coding

A monthly, hands-on session lasting 45 minutes to an hour, in which colleagues share a skill and
everyone gets to run the code themselves. It has run since May 2021 and materials from every session
are published at
[github.com/nhsbsa-data-analytics/coffee-and-coding](https://github.com/nhsbsa-data-analytics/coffee-and-coding).

Past sessions have covered R and Python from scratch, the Open Data Portal API, R Markdown and
official statistics, accessible spreadsheets, and data visualisation. You do not need to be a
confident coder to attend, and you do not need to present to benefit.

For joining details, ask your team lead or the Data Science, Advanced Analytics and Statistics
team.

Collaboration is worth seeking at the start of analysis rather than when you are stuck. It gives
access to skills and knowledge held outside your immediate team, avoids duplication and wasted
effort, avoids conflicting results, and brings a wider range of professional perspectives.[^src-govs-010-section-6-9]

## When the work needs a skill you do not have

Analysis should be undertaken by people with the skills, information and tools the work requires.[^src-govs-010-section-6-8] That is a statement about the work, not a judgement about the analyst, and
it puts an obligation on whoever assigns the work as much as on whoever does it.

**Say so early.** A skills gap found at scoping is a conversation about who else is involved, what
training is needed, or whether the deadline moves. The same gap found at assurance is a finding
against the analysis. Raise it with your team lead, and if it is not resolved there, with the
Analytical Quality and Assurance Lead using the routes above.

**Record it if it is not closed.** Where the work goes ahead without the skill the assurance level
assumes, that is a limitation of the analysis and belongs in the record and in the assurance
statement, the same as any other limitation. See
[section 6](../06-doing-the-work/index.qmd) and
[section 9](../09-communicating-analysis/index.qmd).

Two frameworks help with the wider question of whether NHSBSA has the capability it needs, rather
than with a single piece of work:

| Framework | What it assesses |
|---|---|
| [Statistical Practice Capability Framework](https://osr.statisticsauthority.gov.uk/), Office for Statistics Regulation | How an organisation is developing its statistical practice against Trustworthiness, Quality and Value. It is in development and being trialled with producer bodies, so it is a way of looking at NHSBSA rather than a standard NHSBSA is held to |
| [Government Analytical Evaluation Capabilities Framework](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-magenta-book), a Magenta Book supplementary guide | The competences an evaluation team needs, and how to judge whether it has them |

## Improving this playbook

This playbook is maintained and it is meant to change.

If something here is wrong, unclear, or does not match how work actually happens, say so. That
includes disagreeing with the levels the assurance level decision sheet produces. If it gives an
answer that feels wrong for your work, that is worth reporting: the sheet is only useful if
practitioners recognise its judgements.

Raise it the way you would raise any other change to a repository.
[CONTRIBUTE.md](https://github.com/nhsbsa-data-analytics/nhsbsa-quality-analysis-playbook/blob/main/CONTRIBUTE.md)
explains how, and the pull request template shapes what to include. That is the same route the
Analytical Code Assurance Playbook uses, so the two behave the same way.

## Learning from experience

Identify relevant lessons from previous work when you plan, and capture new ones throughout rather
than reconstructing them at the end.[^src-govs-010-sections-6-7-and-6-10]

Lessons should be evaluated and acted on, not merely recorded, and shared so that others benefit.
Where you have learned something that would help another team, the communities above are the route.
